status.text:
Complaint filed against Krakow police officer who stopped the market-square shooter, demanding a check on the legality of his actions.

On November 7, 2026, 24-year-old Michał Oksyński opened fire near Krakow’s Main Market Square, killing six and wounding 16. 

Officers Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański engaged him, were seriously wounded, but neutralized the attacker, who later died in hospital.

Kulik was hit by three bullets. After one pierced his lung, he reloaded with his left hand and stopped the shooter at close range. He is recovering; the attacker is dead.

A Polish citizen living in London filed a complaint against Kulik, accusing him of excessive force for continuing to shoot after the terrorist was on the ground and seeking details of his death.

Journalists found the complainant’s name and birth details match a man wanted by Polish police for fraud, drunk driving, and threats.

Prosecutors confirmed receipt and will review it, but are not required to open a case if no offense is found. Before the complaint, they saw no grounds to examine the officers’ actions.

Krakow prosecutor Piotr Kosmaty and firearms instructor Dariusz Tomyszek have publicly backed Kulik, saying the weapon remained within the attacker’s reach, so the response was lawful.
